sentences.text: H. Veeramallu vs H. Komuraiah on 14 August, 2024
Author: K. Lakshman

Bench: K. Lakshman  HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K. LAKSHMAN  CIVIL REVISION PETITION Nos.2529 AND 2530 OF 2024 ORAL ORDER:
Heard Mr. M. Rathan Singh, learned counsel for the petitioners and both the revisions are being disposed of at the admission stage itself.

2. C.R.P. No.2529 of 2024 is filed challenging the docket order dated 23.07.2024 in I.A. No.477 of 2024 in A.S. No.48 of 2017 passed by learned Chairman, LRAT - cum - II Additional District Judge,
Karimnagar, dismissing the petition filed under Order - XVII, Rule - 1 read with 151 of CPC to adjourn the appeal Suit for at least three (03) months or till FSL report is received, whereas C.R.P.
No.2530 of 2024 is filed challenging the docket order dated 23.07.2024 in I.A. No.476 of 2024 in A.S. No.47 of 2017 passed by the very same Court dismissing the very same relief sought by the petitioners.

3. Lis involved, the parties in both the revisions are one and the same and, therefore, both the revisions are being heard and disposed of by way of common order.
4.

Originally, the petitioners herein filed a suit vide O.S. No.230 of 2005 against the respondents for declaration of title and KL,J CRP Nos.2529 & 2530 of 2024 recovery of possession in respect of suit schedule property i.e., land admeasuring 226 square yards in Survey No.357/E, situated at Sadasivapally Village of Manakondur Revenue Mandal, Karimnagar District, while O.S. No.231 of 2005 is filed seeking the very same relief in respect of the property admeasuring 216 square yards in the very same survey number.
Vide judgment and decree, dated 27.02.2017, learned II Additional Junior Civil Judge, Karimnagar, dismissed both the suits.

entities.text: II Additional Junior Civil Judge, Karimnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. Challenging the said judgments and decrees, the petitioners preferred appeals vide A.S. Nos.47 and 48 of 2017, respectively.

Therefore,
petitioner No.4 lodged a complaint with Manakonduru Police Station, which in turn registered a case in Crime No.262 of 2022 for the offences under Sections - 420, 468, 471 and 120B read with 34 of IPC.
The police after completion of investigation filed final report stating that the matter is civil in nature.

entities.text:
Special Judicial Magistrate of First Class (Excise),
Karimnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Unless and until the said report is received, it is not possible to proceed with appeal suit.

6. The respondents opposed the aforesaid petitions filed by the petitioners contending that there is delay in filing the petitions and the said crime and FSL report are nothing to do with the present appeals.

7. Vide order dated 23.07.2024, learned appellate Court dismissed the said applications observing thus:
i.

Pursuant to the request made by learned Special Judicial Magistrate of First Class (Excise), Karimnagar, vide official memorandum dated 26.06.2024, the appellate Court handed over Ex.B1 to the Investigating Officer on 26.06.2024 so as to send the same to FSL, Hyderabad.
ii. The said FSL report is to be received by the said Special Judicial Magistrate of First Class (Excise), but not the appellate Court directly to the FSL for comparison.
Therefore, the appellate Court need not wait till receiving FSL report KL,J CRP Nos.2529 & 2530 of 2024 iii.

entities.text: FSL report KL,J CRP Nos.2529 & 2530 of 2024
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On earlier occasions, the Court has granted sufficient time for getting back the original Ex.B1 from FSL.
iv. The appeal suit is old, pertains to the year 2017 and identified matter.
8. Challenging the aforesaid orders, the petitioners filed both these revisions.
9. Perusal of record would reveal that the suits filed by the petitioners vide O.S. Nos.230 and 231 of 2005 were dismissed by the trial Court on 27.02.2017.
Challenging the said dismissal, the petitioners filed appeals vide A.S. Nos.47 and 48 of 2017.
Thus, suits are of the year 2005 and the unregistered partition deed was filed in the suits during trial and it was marked as Ex.B1.

The H. Veeramallu vs H. Komuraiah on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88840434/
2 aforesaid appeals are of the year 2017.
The subject crime i.e., Crime No.262 of 2022 was registered in the year 2022.
Ex . B1
was handed over to Investigating Officer on 26.06.2024.
FSL Report is awaited.
Thus, the petitioners filed the aforesaid Interlocutory Applications vide I.A. Nos.476 and 477 of 2024 in the said appeals after elapse of about more than seven (07) years.

The petitioner set the criminal law on motion in the year 2022 by giving a report with Manakondur Police Station, who in turn registered a case in Crime No.262 of 2022 against KL,J CRP Nos.2529 & 2530 of 2024 the respondent Nos.1 and 2 in C.R.P. No.2529 of 2024 for forging and creating Ex.B1 and using the same as genuine one and sold the suit schedule properties to defendant No.2 causing wrongful loss to the petitioners.
The Investigating Officer after completion of investigation filed a final report stating that the matter is civil in nature.

Thereafter, the petitioners filed a protest petition and the same was allowed and the learned Magistrate directed the Investigating Officer to collect Ex.B1 and send the same to FSL along with admitted signature of deceased petitioner No.1 available on the pattadar passbook No.225461 with Patta No.1122, for comparison and report.

The said report is waiting.
10.

It is the consistent case of the petitioners right from the beginning that Ex.B1 - unregistered partition deed, dated 10.03.1998, under which partition said to have taken place among the brothers i.e., deceased plaintiff No.1, his two brothers and the sons of their predeceased brother, Mr.
Veeraiah.

As per the said document, the suit schedule properties were allotted to defendant No.1,
who in turn sold the same to defendant No.2.

Even then, there is delay on the part of the petitioners in setting the criminal law on motion during pendency of the proceedings in suit and non-filing of a petition before trial Court KL,J CRP Nos.2529 & 2530 of 2024 to send such document to FSL.
There is no explanation from their side in the affidavits filed in support of I.A. Nos.446 and 477 of 2024.

Even otherwise, the appeals were filed in the year 2017 and the petitioners having slept over for about seven (07) years and leisurely filed the aforesaid applications seeking adjournment for want of FSL report.
Thus, the petitioners are not diligent in conducting the proceedings.
On considering the said aspects only, learned appellate Court dismissed both the I.As., and there is no error in it.

Thus,
the revisions fail and the same are liable to be dismissed.
11. It is needless to observe that though there are laches on the part of the petitioners, the same may not be a ground in deciding the rights of the parties in the interest of justice.

It is the contention of the petitioners consistently that deceased plaintiff No.1 never signed on Ex.B1 - partition deed said to have taken place among himself, his two brothers and sons of predeceased brother, Ex.B1 is a vital document which through a light to decide the rights of the parties.
The suit filed by the petitioners is a comprehensive suit involving the rights of the parties over immovable properties.

Therefore, liberty is granted to the petitioners to file an application to lead further evidence on receipt of KL,J CRP Nos.2529 & 2530 of 2024 FSL reports, and the appellate Court is at liberty to consider the same in accordance with law.
12. With the aforesaid observations, both these revisions are disposed of.
But, in the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the revisions shall stand closed.
